body_markdown:
For years, ₱50,000 was the most you could send in a single InstaPay transfer.


Paying a ₱180,000 supplier invoice? Four transfers. Running payroll? Batch it through PESONet and wait, or cut a check. That changed on 29 July 2026.


The BSP and Philippine Payments Management, Inc. (PPMI) raised InstaPay’s per-transaction limit for registered businesses from ₱50,000 to ₱500,000 on the same 24/7 real-time rail.


More money, fewer transfers, same real-time speed.


Here’s what changed, what didn’t, who supports it, what it costs, and what it means for the way your business moves money.


## **What is InstaPay for Business?**


[InstaPay for Business](https://www.rappler.com/business/instapay-raises-transfer-limit-real-time-business-payments/?ref=paymongo-blog.ghost.io) is a higher-limit tier of the InstaPay automated clearing house that lets registered businesses send up to ₱500,000 per transaction in real time, 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It launched on 29 July 2026 and is live from that date, subject to each institution’s own rollout.


It is not a new app or a separate network. It is the same InstaPay rail your business already uses, with the transaction cap lifted tenfold for accounts that qualify. You access it through your bank’s or e-money issuer’s business banking channel.


Two things are worth being precise about:


- **The ₱500,000 limit applies to registered businesses.** The standard ₱50,000 InstaPay transaction limit continues to apply to personal/P2P transfers.
- **It is a credit-push rail.** Your business initiates the payment. It does not pull funds from anyone else’s account. That is what Direct Debit PH, launched the same day, is for.

One caveat that trips up finance teams: the scheme has no daily cap, but your bank does. Originating institutions set their own internal limits, and those are usually lower and often tiered by account type or approval level. Metrobank, for example, raised its retail InstaPay daily limit to ₱100,000 while keeping the per-transaction limit at ₱50,000. Confirm your own limits with your relationship manager before you plan a payment run around ₱500,000 transfers.

## **How InstaPay for Business works**


1. **Qualify.** You need a business or corporate account at a financial institution that offers the facility.
2. **Initiate from your business channel.** Enter the recipient’s institution, account name, and account number, then authorize the transfer. Most institutions require an OTP or a maker-checker approval.
3. **The recipient is credited in real time.** Every transaction generates a reference number you can use for tracking and reconciliation.
4. **Reconcile using the reference number.** Every InstaPay transaction returns a trace or reference number. Keep it; it is your proof of transfer and your audit trail.


The gate is the sending institution. The sending institution needs to support InstaPay for Business. The recipient can receive funds through a participating InstaPay institution.


## **Which banks and e-wallets offer InstaPay for Business**


Five institutions supported InstaPay for Business at launch:


- Philippine National Bank
- Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation (RCBC)
- GoTyme Bank Corporation
- Wise Pilipinas, Inc.
- DCPay Philippines, Inc.


More financial institutions, including major industry players, have expressed interest in offering the facility. For context, InstaPay had 93 participating institutions as of end-2025 – 22 universal and commercial banks, 20 thrift banks, 18 rural banks, five digital banks, and 28 non-bank e-money issuers – so coverage should widen through 2026 and 2027.


If your primary bank is not on the list yet, your practical options are to open a business account at one that is, or keep using PESONet for anything above ₱50,000 until your bank enables it.


## **What InstaPay for Business costs**


Fees are set by the sending institution, not by the scheme. But the pricing environment changed materially in mid-2026.


### **BSP Circular No. 1238 took effect on 4 July 2026**


It requires digital fund-transfer fees to follow a reasonable, fair, market-based pricing framework and be supported by actual processing costs. Digital transfer fees should also remain lower than equivalent over-the-counter charges. BSP has cited an InstaPay switch cost of roughly ₱1.50 as a reference point for the cost of routing an interbank transfer.


The result was a wave of fee removals:


- **BPI** made InstaPay and PESONet transfers permanently free starting 1 July 2026.
- **RCBC** also removed InstaPay fees from eligible digital transfers in July, with terms varying by platform.


Don't assume a retail fee waiver applies to every business or corporate channel. Institutions can price business products separately, so check the fee schedule for your specific account.

## **What this changes for your business, and what it doesn’t**


The ₱500,000 cap is a real improvement to how you send money. Supplier payments, contractor releases, commission payouts, customer refunds, and moving float between your own accounts all get faster and cleaner.


What it does not change is how much a customer can send you in a single InstaPay transaction. Individuals are still capped at ₱50,000. A customer paying you ₱150,000 by manual bank transfer still sends three transfers, generates three reference numbers, and creates three rows for someone on your team to match.


And manual bank transfer has structural gaps that no limit increase fixes:


- **No order attached.** The transfer arrives with a reference number, not an order ID. Matching payment to invoice is manual work.
- **No confirmation your system can act on.** A standard bank transfer does not inherently carry your order ID into your commerce system, nor does the InstaPay network provide a merchant checkout webhook that marks your order as paid.
- **No protection against the wrong amount.** With a manual transfer, the customer enters the amount themselves. Your team still has to handle short payments, overpayments, and duplicate transfers.
- **Manual payment friction.** The customer needs your account details, has to enter the amount themselves, and still has to complete the transfer **.**


If a meaningful share of your revenue arrives as bank transfer screenshots, the limit was never your only bottleneck.

## **Frequently asked questions**


#### ****What is the InstaPay limit for business accounts in 2026?****


The ₱500,000 limit is the scheme-level maximum per transaction. Your bank or e-wallet may impose additional daily, transaction, or approval limits


#### ****Is the personal InstaPay limit still ₱50,000?****


Yes. The ₱500,000 cap applies only to registered business accounts. Personal and person-to-person InstaPay transfers remain capped at ₱50,000 per transaction.


#### ****Which banks offer InstaPay for Business?****


At launch: Philippine National Bank, RCBC, GoTyme Bank, Wise Pilipinas, and DCPay Philippines. Additional financial institutions have expressed interest in offering the facility.


#### Is InstaPay free now?


It depends on your institution. BSP Circular No. 1238, effective 4 July 2026, requires transfer fees to reflect actual processing cost, which led BPI to remove InstaPay and PESONet fees entirely and RCBC to offer 30 free InstaPay transfers per month. Business and corporate channels are priced separately from retail, so confirm the schedule that applies to your account.


#### ****Should I use InstaPay for Business or PESONet?****


Use InstaPay for Business for urgent payments under ₱500,000 that need to arrive immediately, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Use PESONet for bulk payment runs like payroll, or for single payments above ₱500,000 — providers commonly allow up to ₱10 million per transaction, but it settles by clearing cycle on banking days.


#### ****Can my customers pay me more than ₱50,000 in one transaction?****


Not by personal InstaPay transfer — individuals are still capped at ₱50,000. To collect larger amounts in a single transaction, use a payment gateway that supports QR Ph, cards, e-wallets, and direct online banking, with the payment matched to the order automatically.
